Service day close
nodes.rationale: Closing is a ritual, not a flag: refuses while orders open or bills unpaid, freezes totals, frees tables. Since 6.2.3 only bills somebody owes block it; since 6.0.1 a forced close cancels still-open orders before freezing the summary.

nodes.label: Service days (migration v74)
nodes.rationale: Orders filed under a business day instead of UTC date so a service past midnight stays one evening; day opens itself on first order because an offline-first till cannot refuse a ticket; partial unique index guarantees one open day.

nodes.label: Forced day close (owner-only, cancels open orders)
nodes.rationale: Leaving open orders alive on freed tables let last night's check resurface; unpaid bills are not touched because a bill is settled at the till.

nodes.label: Floor map with rooms (migration v75)
nodes.rationale: Rooms become entities measured in abstract units and scaled; since 6.2.1 the scale fits both width and height so the whole room fits the 1024x768 till, falling back to scroll only under 30%.

nodes.label: Horizontal/vertical rectangular table orientation
nodes.rationale: Read back from stored dimensions rather than a separate column; free rotation deliberately dropped.

nodes.label: Reservations (migration v76)
nodes.rationale: Name and head count are all that is needed; reservations belong to the current service, not future dates, because the room is rebuilt daily and tables are deleted.

nodes.label: Reservation sheet with dynamic table assignment
nodes.rationale: POST /reservations/:id/assign is the single operation from which assign, move, swap and release fall out; response says who moved because an invisible swap reads as a bug. no_show distinct from expired.

nodes.label: Joined tables (migration v77, merged_into)
nodes.rationale: One level deep on purpose: no chains to walk and splitting is always one step; order lives on the group leader.

nodes.label: Saved floor plans / table_layouts (migration v78)
nodes.rationale: Layouts store names rather than ids so a plan outlives the emptying of the room; applying rebuilds inside a transaction.

nodes.label: Kitchen tickets sent in rounds (kot_batch, migration v72)
nodes.rationale: order_items.kot_batch registers what already went to the kitchen (NULL = never sent), so print-kot dispatches only pending rows and re-queues only rows of stations that failed.

nodes.label: Orders keep a snapshot of their table (migration v73)
TP801 printer profile (48 cols, code page 16)
WPC1252 code page and NFC normalisation for accents and euro
Kitchen ticket redesign
nodes.rationale: Designed around what the pass reads: table double width, round number, sections per category, notes bold behind >>. Since 6.0.1 identical dishes fold into one line; since 6.0.0 sectioned by service run.

nodes.label: Kitchen ticket has one road (backend only)
nodes.rationale: The browser-drawn ticket printed control codes as garbage and could not stamp the round, so later sends reprinted food; sending always goes through the backend which owns rounds and stations.

nodes.label: Folding identical dishes (ticket, table, bill)
nodes.rationale: Rows stay separate (each has round, run, kitchen state, price); counting happens where it is read. Same product, add-ons in any order, note, variants, price, run and kitchen state fold into one line.

nodes.label: auto_print_kot setting removed
nodes.rationale: A send that silently does nothing leaves the kitchen unaware; kot_printing_enabled remains the single switch.

nodes.label: Customer book switch customers_enabled (migration v79)
nodes.rationale: A restaurant keeping only reservations needs no address book; loyalty switches off with it because the wallet is per customer.

nodes.label: Cloud bridge and telemetry removal (migration v80)
nodes.rationale: Upstream registered with the vendor platform and sent takings, orders and PII on a heartbeat, plus default-on telemetry; all removed and cloud_*/telemetry_* settings cleared, also on backup restore.

nodes.label: Dashboard removal
nodes.rationale: Only statistics; the same numbers appear in the day-close summary by service day, which is the correct definition for a restaurant closing after midnight.

nodes.label: Rename Flo Cafe to BuonApp (it.buonapp.pos, buonapp.local)
nodes.rationale: User data copied from flo-desktop on first launch; database file stays flo.db to keep migration/upgrade paths working.

nodes.label: Services/routes split with no import cycle
nodes.rationale: Reservations needed the service day and day close needed table deletion, causing routes and services to import each other; services hold the domain and routes speak only HTTP.

nodes.label: Windows-only release workflow to GitHub Releases
nodes.rationale: Verifies latest.yml and blockmap for electron-updater; installer unsigned so SmartScreen prompts on first install.

nodes.label: Taxation module removal (migration v81)
nodes.rationale: The install never issues fiscal documents (bill is a preconto, receipt comes from the till), so ~16,000 lines of tax engine, country packs and split-check apportioning were dead weight; historical tax columns on orders/order_items/bills kept to avoid surgery on the money trail.

nodes.label: Receipt-template plugin path removal (migration v82)
nodes.rationale: Templates could only arrive inside tax packs, so the path became unreachable; classic and compact built-in layouts remain.

nodes.label: Clean shutdown and single-instance lock handling
nodes.rationale: Chromium sockets kept http.Server.close() waiting; the timeout aborted cleanup before closeDatabase(). App now cuts its own connections first and WebSocket clients get a grace window.

nodes.label: Order screen (formerly till) takes no money
nodes.rationale: The till is the machine beside the computer; cashing, discounts, voids and preconto moved to where the order lives (table or service day).

nodes.label: Preconto (bill, not a receipt)
nodes.rationale: Printed without a payment window because the floor takes it to the table long before anyone pays; leaves by three roads: thermal, browser ESC/POS encoder, HTML page.

nodes.label: Cover charge (migrations v88-v90)
nodes.rationale: Printed line spells Cover N x price only when the multiplication gives the amount; computed from configured price in cents. A menu including the cover takes its guests off the charge.

nodes.label: Fixed menu (migration v92)
nodes.rationale: A product with a tick that writes real rows, one per dish, because the kitchen ticket sections by category and a package has none; the kitchen never sees the package row.

nodes.label: Per-dish exceptions in menu courses (migration v93)
Fixed menu filled in as the meal goes (migration v95)
nodes.rationale: Courses can be left empty and filled later via PUT /orders/:id/menu-groups/:groupId/courses/:courseId; Required became Expected since a menu can be sent half decided.

nodes.label: Counted fixed menu (menu line with quantity N)
nodes.rationale: The floor writes how many menus then how many of each dish without knowing who eats what; course cap is max_choices x N; no starting number because mixed menu/card tables are common. PATCH menu-groups quantity refuses 409 menu_course_overflow.

nodes.label: Price written on the row (migrations v84, v87)
nodes.rationale: Unpriced rows are flagged explicitly instead of recognised by price zero, which made an intentional zero impossible to confirm.

nodes.label: Split check between guests removed (migration v91)
nodes.rationale: A second billing shape behind one screen; who pays what is settled at the till. v91 merges divided groups back into a single bill before dropping bill_items, split_group_id, split_label and split_checks_enabled. Multi-method payment and unjoining tables stay.

nodes.label: Service runs (migration v94)
nodes.rationale: Which wave of the meal a dish leaves in (1-9), distinct from the round it was sent in; per-category default, labels not gates. Inside a fixed menu the run is not asked or moved since a menu is already an order of runs.

nodes.label: Handheld / Server App (:3003)
nodes.rationale: Rebuilt in 6.0.0 to order the way the central PC does; proxy forwards only what ordering needs and 404s the rest. 6.2.0: dish list instead of tile grid, Handhelds sidebar QR entry, logout revocation persisted.

nodes.label: Any waiter can work any open order
nodes.rationale: The server role used to get 403 on a colleague's order; orders still stamped with user_id, while discounts, prices and payments stay closed to waiters.

nodes.label: New order starts from the table's covers
nodes.rationale: Starting at one charged a table of four as a single cover; uses booking party or seats including joined tables.

nodes.label: Touch UI primitives and status colour tokens
nodes.rationale: 44/48/56 px touch sizes; Modal, SidePanel, PageHeader, Stepper, StatusBadge, SegmentedControl, ActionBar, EmptyState in components/ui; status colours in globals.css and lib/status-styles.ts.

nodes.label: Username login instead of email (migration v96)
nodes.rationale: BuonApp sends no mail and emails were invented to pass the form; users.email renamed to users.username in place, keeping the local part of the email so nobody learns a new name.

nodes.label: Persisted token revocation on handheld logout
nodes.rationale: In-memory revocation was lost on restart, leaving a signed-out token valid up to ten days over plain HTTP Wi-Fi.

nodes.label: WhatsApp switched off via WHATSAPP_AVAILABLE
nodes.rationale: Nobody uses it and it was never tried on a real till; code, tables and tests kept, /api/whatsapp unmounted (404).

nodes.label: Cached C# DLL for USB raw ESC/POS printing on Windows
nodes.rationale: Add-Type recompiled the helper per ticket (~10 s on a Celeron); compiled once to a hash-named DLL in background at launch, falling back to inline compile; WMI query only on failure.

nodes.label: Window sized to display work area (1024x768 till)
nodes.rationale: createWindow() asked 1400x900 and Windows did not shrink it, so the till saw only the top-left corner; below 1400x900 it starts maximised.
